embeddings.title: Silver Valley
embeddings.description:
Silver Valley is a transformative system comprising an in-game experience and an after-game alternate reality game (ARG) experience. The primary objective of this project is to rebuild the connections between the older and younger generations, addressing the disconnection that often arises in our rapidly advancing technological landscape.

The motivation for undertaking this project stemmed from a realization that modern technology has largely overlooked the unique needs and perspectives of the elderly. I was compelled to contribute to changing this situation by designing an experience that would facilitate intergenerational communication and understanding.

In the immersive in-game experience of Silver Valley, players are transported to a magical world where they assume the roles of animal characters, each representing distinct personalities and perspectives. The project revolves around the collection of real stories through interviews with silver hair individuals, which become the foundation for the in-game content. These authentic experiences and personal histories serve as a catalyst for creating a captivating storytelling environment that resonates with players Through engaging gameplay and captivating storytelling, players are invited to explore the lives and stories of these characters, fostering empathy and connection.

However, the experience extends beyond the confines of the game. The after-game ARG experience plays a vital role in amplifying the impact of Silver Valley. It encourages players to share real stories of the elderly within their own families and communities, effectively bridging the virtual and real worlds to foster dialogue, reflection, and the celebration of diverse narratives.

embeddings.title: Kleshas
embeddings.description:
Kleshas is a generative art made by Unity and it runs on a PC controlled by PICO 4 VR device. After wearing the VR device, users can see mainly five kinds of creatures flowing in the virtual space. Each of them performs different behaviors based on the theory of “Kleshas”(Attachment, Anger, Ignorance, Pride and Doubt). Also, emotion creatures have different materials and shapes. These five creatures are randomly generated and they compose an ecosystem. Audience can observe this environment on the VR platform. 

I am very interested in Buddhism, especially its interpretation of Kleshas(affliction or poison in English). Kleshas are the root of human’s unhappiness so i want to imitate a society that is filled with these negative emotions. When users dive into the virtual world, they will see a beautiful and harmonious environment that finally turns to be chaotic and disordered. By doing so, I hope my manifestation of negative emotions can let people reflect on themselves. We all have negative emotions in our daily life, however, we need to stop spreading our negative energy to others.

embeddings.title: Excavating Eternal Beings - A Past Life Regression
embeddings.description: Audiovisual installation telling the story of my future incarnation on a past life regression, discovering the patterns throughout 9 lifetimes and continuing her life journey with a change. The video consists of 11 scenes total, a prologue, an epilogue, and 9 scenes in between. It is a personal project exploring my own psyche.

embeddings.title: Daydreams of Simulacra (Hallucinated Voicemail)
embeddings.description: Daydreams of Simulacra is an audio sculpture that uses artificial intelligene to reflect simulated conversation and human connection back to the audience. By engaging with the piece’s multi-channel speaker chamber, the viewer is confronted with an overwhelming chorus of communication simulacra and prompted to explore the textures of the created audioscape.

embeddings.title: Don’t Look At Me When I’m Coding
embeddings.description:
In an age of artificial intelligence, perhaps we are the last generation of manual coders. This art installation captures the essence of our craft and the spirit of the artisan in coding, particularly focusing on the amusing reality that I become uncomfortable when others watch me code. The installation involves two laptops: one displaying a replay of my coding process which halts as soon as an audience observes it, mirroring my own behavior when coding under watchful eyes.

Behind this laptop, a second machine churns out AI-generated code, but with an intriguing twist. It only generates code when observed, standing in stark contrast to the human vulnerability and embarrassment that halts the first machine. This stark dichotomy is designed to highlight the unique human qualities that persist even in an AI-dominated era.

The exhibit poses an important question to its audience: In the age of AI, what should we preserve and what should we update? This isn’t just an exploration of the craft of coding; it's a conversation starter about the future of humanity and the intersection of AI and human emotions. It pays homage to the fact that even in a world inundated with AI, the human factor remains integral and irreplaceable.

embeddings.title: Body Domain
embeddings.description:
"Body Domain" is an interactive installation piece that invites participants to engage in a unique dance experience. Within the installation space, participants are prompted by animations to create movements that generate image sequence. 

These visuals intentionally shifts the focus from the participant's identity to the dynamics of their movements. Through this transformative visual representation, both participants and audiences are immersed in a shared experience. The installation creates a captivating space where the boundaries between performer and observer blur, encouraging participants to explore the artistry of movement.

embeddings.title: Before the Sun Rises
embeddings.description: Before the Sun Rises is an online multiplayer game designed to encourage altruistic and prosocial behavior between strangers. In the current landscape of primarily competitive multiplayer games, how do we design a game that encourages kind, compassionate and generous behavior, but also provides a sense of agency while doing so?

embeddings.title: Nesting: The Non-Human Technology of Bird Nests
embeddings.description: I spent several weeks studying the nest-building behavior of birds, examining the ways in which they build homes and the technologies they have developed in order to do so. This began as an exercise in considering how a specific non-human species, birds, intelligently solves craft-based problems, and became an emotive exploration of the elements that creatures – human and non-human alike — use to build homes.

embeddings.title: I Made A Miro Board
embeddings.description: This thesis is about navigating the duality of truth in an era that is getting harder and harder to make friends and communicate honestly without offending anyone.  While the questions asked in my thesis journey might have been more specific to my personal upbringing and encounters, the projects made throughout the thesis journey are a series of experiments utilizing interactive media tools to find a way to foster deliberative democracy better.

embeddings.title: Sleepy Paradise
embeddings.description:
My thesis project surrounds the topic of enhancing elderly’s mental wellbeing - particularly on how a digital application can help them relieve anxiety, improve mood and sleep well. The product delivers an audio-visual experience, aiming to provide elderly the access to specific video content (a combination of nature therapy and music therapy). 

My intention comes from my grandparents as recently they are starting to live alone sometimes, and post-COIVD they faced a change to their lifestyle - spending more time at home and feeling less sense of companionship. My grandma also told me her sleep quality is getting worse. She sometimes has to rely on melatonin to fall asleep quicker, and also tend to wake up in the middle of night. How might they sleep better, and feel less anxious, bored, lonely at home? Because of my close connection with my grandparents, I want to use my previous knowledge and experience on product design, in addition to what I learned from this master’s program on interactive media, to create something meaningful and make their daily lives better & healthier. This might sound more of a personal project, but I hope what I designed can also benefit other elders with similar needs. 

Another intention is that I want to explore the topic of technology on the elder generation, especially how we can use technology to its most optimal extent so that elders would not feel overwhelmed. Therefore, this project not only focuses on the curation of effective video content but also explores user interface design and the format of display. The product form is a digital application with 2 types of interfaces: mobile touch screen and TV with remote control. They both provide access to beautiful nature videos with instrumental music and nature sounds. I programmed in p5.js using the machine learning method to add in a voice-control function where the elderly can choose which type of nature sounds they want to listen to. The code runs in the background; so while the video and music are continuously playing, different nature sounds (birds, wind, rain, etc.) can tune in anywhere based on their voice command.

embeddings.title: Ecstasy and Dissolution
embeddings.description:
After 4 years of performing brainwave-powered techno, I came to NYU to research a number of consciousness-expanding experiences that emerged spontaneously during my shows. I reviewed my journal entries and video recordings of those shows, honing in on the use of repetitive beats. I researched how they impact consciousness and performed experiments where I listened to the same beat for an hour and observed an increase in “theta” brainwave levels. This increase indicates a trance state where the brain is dreaming yet still awake. I designed a soundscape protocol that induces a theta state. Finally, I performed a series of soundbaths using sounds from my live heart and brainwave data. These experiences entrained the audience members to my biometrics and guided them into elusive states of consciousness.  

I was drawn to this work because of the intimacy of live biofeedback. When I performed techno in the past - as long as I pressed the keys at the right time - no one knew what I was feeling. With biofeedback music, the audience knows. This vulnerability is a refreshing contrast to the dehumanization I typically feel when using technology.

I’m also interested in this work because of its power to recreate elusive states of consciousness without the use of mind-altering drugs. During my childhood, I felt safer being in my head rather than in the real world, which was sometimes dangerous. Imagination, fantasy, and music were safe places for me. In my late teens I became a “psychonaut,” exploring the far reaches of my mind with drug use. My music also reflected this, using experimental compositions to push the listener’s mind. At age 20, I found meditation, another exploratory tool. These methods satisfied a deep curiosity of the unknown and a desire to master my mind, thoughts, and emotions.

embeddings.title: Delete Me
embeddings.description:
We live in an era of cheap digital storage, online-first everything, and widespread use of artificial intelligence. Personal data collection has become excessive, and with it - I believe we face an increased risk of harm.  The more we rely on the internet, the more data governments and companies accumulate about us. At the same time, their ability to process that data quickly, cheaply, and intelligently is improving rapidly with recent advancements in A.I. 
 
Earlier in my career, I worked on news feed personalization at Facebook.  The models that I helped build there would train on a user's entire history of interactions (every click, scroll, and view from Facebook, Instagram, any website with a Facebook cookie). We developed a best-in-class understanding of our users' interests. These "interest profiles" - as we called them - help Facebook deliver hyper personalized content to keep people scrolling. Over time, I became increasingly uncomfortable with the impact of my work and concerned with how widespread “surveillance capitalism” has become. Addictive technology and invasive targeting has the power to control people, communities, and democracies.

Big data is invisible and (in the US) the entities that aggregate, manipulate, and sell information about us are also often invisible. Because digital rights regulation in the United States is severely lacking, managing one’s vast and distributed volume of personal data can feel hopeless. 

This work is an attempt to manifest my own digital footprint into a physical form for the sole purpose of imagined destruction. My hope is that “Delete Me” not only has the power to educate viewers on the scale and distributed nature of mass data collection in the United States, but that its interactive components also provide an emotional outlet for those of us wrestling with the impracticality of digital privacy in modern society.

embeddings.title: Classifier
embeddings.description: This project presents an innovative physical installation designed to provoke contemplation on the intricate nature of emotions. By employing a camera and a facial emotion recognition system, the installation records and analyzes individuals who participate, generating comprehensive prediction reports encompassing attributes such as age, gender, race, emotion, mental health, and overall score. These reports are printed out using a continuous printer, and individuals are assigned scores based on a meticulously developed algorithm. Participants can choose to take away the report or pin it on the wall for reference. The primary objective of this project is to encourage a deeper understanding of emotions by considering their diverse expressions and the potential risks associated with facial emotion recognition technology and artificial intelligence biases. Furthermore, it prompts critical questioning regarding the necessity of utilizing facial emotion recognition to predict inner feelings, assess dependability, conscientiousness, emotional intelligence, and cognitive ability, thereby envisioning a future where every facial expression is automatically analyzed.

embeddings.title: FutureCraft: A Collaborative World Building System
embeddings.description:
FutureCraft is a collaborative future world building card game designed to explore the potential consequences of our decisions and build a better future together. This game uses AR technology to visualize the future world created by players, making it a dynamic and engaging experience that encourages players to think critically about the world around them.

In FutureCraft, players assume the role of architects of the future, working together to build a world based on their collective decisions. Each player must consider the impact of their choices on four key areas: economy, environment, society, and technology. By reflecting on the world they've built, players can gain valuable insights into the complex interplay of factors that shape our world and learn more about their own decision-making process.

The game is designed for 2-4 players, and encourages collaboration, role-playing, and strategic thinking. Each game session is unique, as the decisions made by players will determine the outcome of the future world they create. This makes the game not only engaging, but also highly informative and thought-provoking.

FutureCraft is an ideal tool for anyone interested in exploring the future and the impact of our decisions on the world around us. Whether you're a student, a researcher, or simply a curious individual looking to gain a deeper understanding of the world, this game is sure to provide a valuable and engaging experience.

embeddings.title: The Wheel of Anxiety
embeddings.description:
"The Wheel of Anxiety" is a web experience that invites participants to engage with a mesmerizing visual graphic consisting of texts and symbolic representations of "Anxiety." It explores the relationship between individuals and the pervasive and unavoidable Anxiety in contemporary Chinese society.

Anxiety is always there and cannot be eradicated. The more one focuses on it, the more confusion and unrest it brings. Why not, instead, cease the gaze?

embeddings.title: Interactive Theatre in the Digital Age
embeddings.description: What began as an exploration of a low tech form of interactive theatre (Theatre of the Oppressed) evolved into performing Theatre of the Oppressed with digital engagement, using live streams and VR. Theatre of the Oppressed seeks to blur the lines between audience and actor through active participation; empowering the audience to be able to make a change both in the art that they consume and in the world around them. My goal with the digital engagement is to broaden the reach of this kind of work--work that has proved to be a powerful and subversive tool in a live format--and to enable those outside of the physical space where it's performed to take part in it.

embeddings.title: Merging Worlds: bridging analog and digital photography
embeddings.description:
This project embarks on a personal journey, intertwining my passion for analog photography with my identity as a software engineer. For the longest time, I believed these two realms were mutually exclusive, forcing me to make a choice between them. However, through my involvement in the IMA Low Res program, I began to see the shades of gray between the black and white. I envisioned a world where my passions could harmoniously coexist.
The spark of inspiration ignited when I decided to reimagine my most treasured possession—the camera. Drawing inspiration from the cherished analog models that have influenced my craft, I set out to design a camera that uses the tactile allure of analog cameras but also seamlessly integrates digital capabilities. It would use a waist-level viewfinder to serve as the primary interface for framing photos. But concealed within is a Raspberry Pi, discreetly capturing images in digital form.
However, my exploration extended beyond the hardware itself. I delved deep into the realms of photography theory and the psychology behind sharing images on social media platforms. As someone who predominantly shares their work online, I was often disheartened by the battle against algorithms to gain visibility and validation. The relentless pursuit of likes and followers began to overshadow the intrinsic value of my creations. I wanted to redefine the way I share my work.
Thus, alongside the camera, I designed and built a website to display the photos taken from my camera. Instead of a polished and professional portfolio, I aimed for a space that encourages authenticity and rawness of my everyday moments. Inspired by experimental web design, I infused elements of skeuomorphism to instill a sense of tangibility in the digital realm.

embeddings.title: Beyond The Spectrum
embeddings.description: Beyond The Spectrum is an immersive, illustrative experience that uses a projector, chalk footsteps, audio, and illustrations as a way to pay homage to the African American figures that paved the way artistically for myself and others! I wanted to create this experience because I did not want their stories to be swept under the rug and forgotten. I chose to include my Grandparents at the end of my thesis because they too have experienced a lot as it pertains to skin color, and how that was used as a divisive factor during the 1950s-1980s. I felt it was important to tell their story and to make sure that the audience heard their voices as well! During a time where the color of their skin meant a lot, each of these individuals I chose to showcase all had to push against a system that was trying to silence them and their artistic visions. Their ability to break through that wall, created an artistic explosion, and a movement that transcended past skin color. Their boldness now allows myself and others to freely express ourselves.

embeddings.title: Self Talk to Self Confidence: Inspiring Women through Positive Affirmations
embeddings.description:
This project aims to create a community where women can share positive self-talk that helps them feel supported and empowered and teach them new phrases and ways of thinking that help them feel more connected and less alone.

Positive self-talk and manifesting have become buzz topics in recent years. The rise of lifestyle brands, self-help sites, and positive affirmation apps like Goop and I Am have helped bring self-care and affirmations into the mainstream. While these strive to empower women and provide them with tools for overcoming work stress and anxiety, the rise of the controversial “Girl Boss” culture has also left many feeling less confident and worse about themselves. I decided to do a deep dive into positive affirmations to see their efficacy as a confidence and self-esteem-boosting tool and how often women use them.

I started by sending a survey to dozens of women in my life. Reading through their responses, I found a common trend: women use their versions of affirmations and positive talk to combat negative feelings of imposter syndrome, stress, and anxiety. What was most shocking was how many of them struggled with imposter syndrome, how much their struggles resonated with me, and how their affirmations and self-talk made me feel more equipped to deal with the challenges in my life. 

As a starting point, I settled on creating a community-oriented website to connect women and allow them to share their insights and affirmations with other women. I was also intrigued by the idea that many of these women had created affirmations that could be even more impactful and effective with slight modifications to their wording and structure. This insight led to research into the semantics of affirmations, particularly phrasing, structuring, and repetition. I found a set of guidelines using wisdom from multiple sources within the psychology and self-help world and decided to make education a core component of my site. 

I began making wireframes and mockups of layouts, font choices, text, color schemes, and imagery to create an aesthetic and identity for my website. I sent these designs to friends and shared them with the IMA Low Res class to get their feedback and hone in on an approachable, user-friendly, and relaxing aesthetic. One friend recommended using music to craft a calming, mindful environment, so I found soothing soundtracks online to add as ambiance.

Overall, I am happy with the current look and feel of the site. My next steps for this project are: to create a functioning mockup of the site to allow for further user testing and improvement and to investigate the challenges of content moderation, community building, and community management.

embeddings.title: lush foliage and flourishing branches
embeddings.description: If a man who suffered from dementia lost all his memories and the identities such as being a grandfather, father, and husband in the last stage of his life, is he already dead although he was still alive physically?

embeddings.title: Reduce Your Time Waste
embeddings.description:
In the digital age, people fall into the trap of wasting excessive time online, leading to unhappiness and discontentment. The allure of social media, streaming platforms, and endless sources of entertainment has blurred the line between intentional and habitual internet use, resulting in a neglect of offline experiences and a negative impact on well-being.

Endless scrolling through social media feeds, binge-watching TV shows, and succumbing to clickbait articles have become commonplace time sinks. Doom scrolling and time wasted surfing the web increase feelings of loneliness, depression, and anxiety. The constant exposure to carefully curated online personas can trigger a sense of inadequacy and negatively impact self-esteem. 

The core of this project is to reframe our relationship with time and prioritize meaningful offline experiences and intentional online use. It aims to inspire individuals to reclaim their time by setting boundaries and goals for screen time and offering tools to help spend time doing offline activities that promote human connection, hobby building and growth, and physical activity. Actively allocating time to hobbies, outdoor pursuits, and face-to-face interactions creates a more fulfilling and balanced life.

By embracing a mindful approach to time management and shifting the focus from the virtual world to the real world, this project empowers individuals to live fuller lives offline, nurturing their mental, emotional, and physical well-being. Through these efforts, people can rediscover the joys of genuine human connection and enrich their lives beyond the confines of the digital realm.

embeddings.title: Perceptible Radio Waves
embeddings.description:
Society has seen a drastic shift in how humans communicate since the advent of wireless telecommunications. Many of these technologies, such as cellular data and WiFi, use radio waves to transmit data through the air. These imperceptible waves are ubiquitous in our lives, yet how often do we consider the physical material that our modern wireless world is built upon?

Perceptible Radio Waves is an exploratory project that aims to break down the abstractions of telecommunications to a physical representation of the phenomenon that they are built upon, namely radio waves. The ultimate goal is to figure out if engaging with radio waves through artistic practice can allow individuals to gain a deeper, more intuitive understanding of what radio waves are.

The main output of the project is a Perceptible Radio Device that guides an audience in observation of the physical space around them. Through guided audio, the audience is encouraged to consider that which they can perceive in the air through their senses, such as the temperature, the and quality of the light. They are then asked to compare that experience with the imperceptible activity that is also occurring in their space, specifically focusing on the radio waves oscillating all around them.
In addition to the guided audio, the device is also observing FM radio signals in real-time, and translates those signals into changing light patterns, revealing the invisible activity occurring in the air.

embeddings.title: Seatizen?
embeddings.description: The theme of my thesis project is global climate change and rising sea levels, focusing on the gradual loss of habitable land for humans. I have created a series of artworks depicting a story where the sea engulfs the last piece of land on Earth, forcing humanity to live in the ocean. In my research, I have extensively studied the effects of climate change leading to rising sea levels, and I have become aware of the severity of environmental destruction. However, over the past three years, the pandemic has led to reduced human travel, slowed trade and production, resulting in some positive trends in environmental data. While the reality of environmental damage cannot be completely reversed, I believe that if everyone pays attention and takes appropriate measures, improvements can be made. That's why I created this interactive art installation, which I hope to showcase in a park during the summer in New York. Through a visually compelling way, I aim to remind people to cherish the environment—it's not too late to act.

embeddings.title: Black is Beautiful
embeddings.description: My project is an interactive museum on the “Black is Beautiful” movement in the 1960s and today. It is not only for black people but for all, to create a nostalgic feeling that clothing has and what identity it holds with each of us.

embeddings.title: The starry sky
embeddings.description: When I stand under the starry sky, I feel its tranquility and vastness, its loneliness and charm. I try to integrate these complex emotions into my works of art, hoping to arouse the viewer's deep thinking about the universe and self-existence. Feel the poetry and brilliance of those distant stars, fly under the wings of art, transcend the constraints of reality, and welcome the infinite possibilities of the universe. The starry sky always brings the source of fantasy to people from ancient times to the present. It is an important source of inspiration for human beings. It is becoming more and more difficult to get in touch with the starry sky in the current urban life. I hope that I can make a starry sky by myself, a breathing starry sky, to hug you.

embeddings.title: Last Night Memory
embeddings.description:
Last Night Memory is an interactive film that contains traditional film screening, AR, and VR experiences. The project uses three different methods of storytelling to show one story in three views: third-person (film), first-person(AR), and the character's mental world(VR). 

The story is about a murder in a family, and is told in a way of "flashback memory". Memory tends to be blurry and ambiguous, so it comes in fragments. The truth appears when all fragments are connected.

embeddings.title: Salsa Y Cafe
embeddings.description: My project entails the exploring the connection between physical media and digital media and how this connection can create an immersive experience for the user that teaches them about something new through a comforting environment. The topic I want to teach about is salsa dancing/music since it's such a personal space for me and the comforting environment I am creating is through a cozy coffee shop. I hope that this experience can encourage the user to find community around them or even appreciate whatever other community they are part of.

embeddings.title: Haptic Memory
embeddings.description:
Reflect on an embarrassing moment from your past. 
Do you feel the cringe in your body when it's recalled? 
What is that feeling?

Haptic Memory is an immersive experience that connects audio narratives with haptic reactions to bring awareness to our memories' mind/body connection and greater impact on our lives over time.
Sometimes, those memories are so traumatic that we disassociate. What is it like to reintroduce that memory and notice your body's hidden protective behaviors?

Other times, those memories are so sweet they become the pinnacle of how we measure our happiness. Even if the people associated are no longer relevant in our lives, why do our bodies hold on to the feeling? 
 
The prototype of Haptic Memory investigates our common psychosomatic sensations, brought to life through Arduino and wireless computation rigged into a wearable vest. The sensations aim to authentically express the depth of these stories where words fall short. 

No matter the narrator's experience, similar sensations reoccurred in the process of haptic scoring: racing heart, ringing in the ears, change in temperature, and butterflies in the stomach -- leading to expansive questions about the universal processes of internalizing past experiences beyond the imagination.  

Anonymous participants for this project graciously provided their personal narratives to be experienced and scored with their matching sensations.

embeddings.title: With/In No Particular Order
embeddings.description: PESCA is a network of nodes that communicate with each other to show different arrangements of individuals in groups as they occur. It is a manifestation of the quiet observation of a hopeful artist, curious about the nature of making choices in an world with an ever changing framework.
